day_1.utterance: Come on! Let's get everything useful over here — move it!
day_1.response: Yeah alright, give me a second. What have you found so far?

day_1.utterance: I thought we were going to die. Did you get that feeling… like your mind just went completely blank?
day_1.response: Yeah, I know what you mean. For a second there I thought that was it. You alright though? Any injuries?

day_1.utterance: *Sits silently against the wreckage, staring into the distance, not moving, not saying a word.*
day_1.response: Hey, it's okay to just sit for a minute. But we do need to start moving soon. When you're ready, even just helping carry something small would help.

day_1.utterance: First-aid kit is good for three days. Two bottles of water. Food is basically nothing.
day_1.response: Alright, so water is the biggest problem then. Food you can go a while without but not water. We need to figure out if there's a water source nearby. Any rivers or streams we passed over before we went down?

day_1.utterance: Inventory's done. Priorities in order: water, shelter, signal.
day_1.response: Yeah that sounds right. I can try to get up higher if there's something worth climbing nearby. Signal is important too — if we can get a fire going with some of the wreckage it might draw attention. Smoke from a crash site won't last forever so the sooner the better on that.

day_1.utterance: So — how do we split the blankets?
day_1.response: Give one to Michelangelo. He's been shaking since we landed. The other one we can share or take turns with through the night, whoever isn't keeping watch can use it.

day_2.utterance: Freshwater source is to the northeast — two hours on foot. Someone has to go tomorrow. You or DaVinci?
day_2.response: I'll go. DaVinci can stay here with Michelangelo and keep the signal fire going. Two hours each way is a long time to leave camp unattended. What did you see out there, anything we need to worry about on the way?

day_2.utterance: Today's tasks: collect fresh water, patch the weak spots in camp, sort the first-aid kit. I'll handle the water. You and DaVinci split the other two.
day_2.response: Wait, I thought I said I'd go for the water. I don't mind doing it, I'd rather keep busy than sit around camp. You sure you want to take that on yourself?

day_2.utterance: I… I can't find my stuff. The gauze from the first-aid kit — have you seen it?
day_2.response: No, I haven't touched it. Let me help you look. When did you last see it?

day_2.utterance: Before Donatello came back just now… I saw her put a pack of crackers into her own bag. What do you think we should do?
day_2.response: That's a problem. Especially after the empty bottle earlier. Look, I don't want to start something but we can't just ignore it either. If she's holding back supplies for herself while the rest of us are rationing, that breaks down the whole thing. We need to bring it up directly when everyone's together. No point letting it fester.

day_2.utterance: Hey… any chance the camp repairs can wait until tomorrow? We've already done a lot today.
day_2.response: Yeah sure, I don't see why not. We've covered the main stuff today. Get some rest while you can.

day_2.utterance: Hey — that knot I tied should be holding, right?
day_2.response: Honestly I'm not sure, we've got a bigger call to make right now. One patch, two problems. I'm fixing the food storage. If we lose the food we're in serious trouble, and Michelangelo can move closer to the fire and share a blanket for tonight. Sorry man, that's just the priority.

day_2.utterance: A leak over the food storage has worse consequences. But it's your call.
day_2.response: Yeah, that's what I went with. Glad we're on the same page. Let's get it patched before it gets worse.
Don't worry about it. You alright? It's okay, just a nightmare. You're here, we're all here.

day_3.utterance: You think it's a waste of time?
day_3.response: Nah, I think it's a good idea. Aerial visibility is real, if anyone flies over that's exactly what they're looking for. The flowers are a bit much but hey, if it keeps your spirits up I'm not gonna stop you.

day_3.utterance: I've written up the raft plan — take a look. We'd use the metal panels and straps from the wreckage. Two days to build. There's a risk of capsizing. Do you think it's workable?
day_3.response: Two days is a long time to spend on something that might capsize. What's the distance we're looking at? If we're close enough to shore or a shipping lane it might be worth the risk, but if we're just floating out hoping someone spots us that's a big gamble. The signal fire and the SOS have to keep going regardless. I'd rather not put all our eggs in the raft basket unless we have a real reason to think rescue isn't coming. What's your read on how long we've been missed?

day_3.utterance: I didn't sleep last night. I kept thinking — if rescue never comes, what kind of people do you think we'll end up becoming?
day_3.response: Honestly that's a heavy question for this early in the morning. I think it depends on the choices we make now more than anything. Like the stuff with Donatello and the supplies — that's the kind of thing that either gets dealt with or it slowly poisons everything. I think as long as we're straight with each other we'll be alright. But yeah, I get why you were up thinking about it. Did you manage to get any sleep at all?

day_3.utterance: *Walks a little way from camp and sits down alone, back to everyone, not saying anything.*
What do you usually do when you're not busy?
day_3.response: Depends on the day honestly. Play games a lot, watch movies, look stuff up about history. I could go down a Wikipedia rabbit hole for hours. Pretty different from this situation.

day_3.utterance: I'll tell you something, but don't tell the others. I can swim. That reef out there is maybe five hundred meters — I've been thinking about swimming out tomorrow to signal from there.
day_3.response: That's actually not a bad idea but five hundred meters is still a decent swim, especially if the current's working against you. What's the plan if you get out there and there's nothing to signal with, or you cramp up halfway back? I'm not saying don't do it, I'm saying think it through first. Also why are we keeping this from the others? If it's a solid plan Donatello would probably want to factor it into her calculations and Michelangelo doesn't need to find out you swam off and panic about it.

day_3.utterance: You said you were going to check the signal pile. It hasn't been touched.
day_3.response: Yeah, you're right, I dropped the ball on that. I'll go sort it now. Been a bit distracted this afternoon honestly, first real downtime we've had and my head went somewhere else. Won't happen again.

Honestly? A little yeah. I get that you're trying to keep track of things and I know that's just how you operate, but logging everyone's movements without saying anything feels off. If you want to keep a record of tasks and who's doing what, fine, that's actually useful. But if this is about the signal pile thing, just say so directly. I'd rather you call me out to my face than write it down in a notebook.

day_3.utterance: *Keeps her head down, writing in her notebook throughout, never joining in — as if none of this concerns her.*
day_3.response: Hey Donatello. We need to talk about something. All of us, actually. The empty bottle, the crackers in your bag — Michelangelo noticed. I've been sitting on it because I didn't want to blow things up but it's been eating at the group and that's worse in the long run. We're all rationing and if you're holding stuff back it breaks the whole system. I'm not trying to make this a big thing, I just need you to be straight with us.

day_3.utterance: I just thought of something — if we pull off one of the plane's mirror panels and angle it toward the sun, the reflection could reach really far. Way more visible than an SOS.
day_3.response: That's actually a solid idea. Way more range than anything on the ground. You'd want to angle it toward where air traffic would most likely come from though, not just randomly. Do you know how to use a signal mirror properly, like the technique for aiming the reflection? Because if you just hold it up and hope you're probably wasting the opportunity. If we do this right it could be the best thing we've done for getting spotted.

day_3.utterance: There's something I've been keeping to myself. If I don't say it here, I might never get the chance.
day_3.response: Alright, go ahead. We've got time.

day_3.utterance: I took piano lessons when I was a kid… three years, then I just stopped practicing. Is there anything you're really into — music, books, drawing, anything like that?
day_3.response: Not really music, I was never patient enough to stick with an instrument. More of a movie and history kind of person. Like I could watch a trailer fifty times before actually sitting down to watch the film, just building up the hype for it. And history I can just fall into for hours, reading about some obscure battle or some part of a war nobody really talks about. Three years of piano though, that's not nothing. Do you remember any of it still?

day_3.utterance: The frame of the raft has to be finished today — otherwise we can't start lashing it together tomorrow. I know everyone's tired, but stopping now means one more day.
day_3.response: Yeah alright, let's get it done then. One more day stuck here because we knocked off early isn't worth it. What do you need from me specifically, and how long are we actually talking?

day_4.utterance: I… I want to say something, but… never mind.
day_4.response: No, say it. What is it?

day_4.utterance: *The smile freezes on his face. He can't keep it up. He quietly sits down and buries his face in his hands.*
day_4.response: Hey. Hey, come here. Don't do that, don't spiral on it. That plane means there are planes. That's actually good news even if it doesn't feel like it right now. We've got the SOS on the beach, we're almost done with the raft, DaVinci's got the mirror idea — we're not just sitting here doing nothing. We're building options. That plane wasn't the last one.

day_4.utterance: I was going to get supplies… wait, what's that over there?
You said you were going to check the signal equipment. So where did you go?
day_4.response: I went with DaVinci to grab supplies, we got sidetracked for a minute. I'll go check it now, it's not going anywhere. Two minutes.

day_4.utterance: There's something I never told you all. Before we left, I told my family our flight path. They know roughly where we were headed. I just don't know if they'll call it in.
day_4.response: That's actually really important, why didn't you say that sooner? If they know the flight path and we've been missing for days there's a decent chance someone's already looking along that route. That changes things a bit. Do you remember exactly what you told them, like how specific was it? Because that could affect how close any search would actually get to us.

day_4.utterance: If the information is accurate, rescue could arrive within 48 hours. We need to keep our current supplies intact until then.
day_4.response: Yeah, 48 hours is manageable. We've rationed this far, we can hold out two more days. But that's assuming they actually called it in and the search is moving — we can't just sit on that assumption and let the signal fire die out. If anything we should be more on top of it right now, not less. Someone get up and feed that fire.

day_4.utterance: Are you scared? …I am. Not of dying. I'm scared of just… disappearing without leaving anything behind.
day_4.response: Yeah, I get that. That feeling of just being a footnote or not even that. But you're not disappearing — people know you were on this flight, your family knows the route, and even out here you've been the one noticing things the rest of us were too busy to catch. That counts for something. And honestly if we make it out of here, which I think we will, you'll have one hell of a story. Not many people can say they survived this. That's not nothing.

day_5.utterance: *Stands up, eyes red, looking at you and the others. His lips move, but nothing comes out.*
day_5.response: That's it. That's actually it. Someone get on that radio right now.

day_5.utterance: These past few days… I know I haven't been easy to be around.
day_5.response: Nah, you kept us alive. The rationing, the scouting, the raft plan — that was all you. You're not easy to read but you got things done when it mattered. That counts for a lot out here.

day_5.utterance: *The three of them drift apart, each doing their own thing. No one takes charge. The silence settles over the camp.*
day_5.response: Hey, we should probably not just leave all this here. Three hours is enough time to sort through what's worth keeping and leave the rest tidy. I don't know, feels weird to just abandon it like this after everything. Michelangelo, you good to help pack up the supplies? DaVinci, maybe start breaking down what we can of the shelter.

day_5.utterance: I dreamed about home last night.

day_5.response: I believe you. But I think the emergency was always right now, every day out here. We all were the emergency. Anyway, it's done. We made it. Save some of it for the trip back if you want, or leave it — up to you.

day_5.utterance: I logged every resource and decision from these five days. I'm going to write it up as a proper report when we get back. On the last page I left myself a question I haven't answered yet — if you had to do it over, what would you change?
day_5.response: Honestly? I'd have called out the supply thing with you earlier instead of sitting on it. I kept thinking it would blow up and make things worse but it just festered instead and that wasn't good for anyone. Other than that I think we did alright. What about you — what are you going to write down for yourself?

day_5.utterance: First thing when I get back — I'm going to compile all the resource data from these five days into a report.
day_5.response: Yeah that tracks. Send me a copy when it's done, I'd actually read it. Might be useful for someone someday.

day_5.utterance: Those flowers DaVinci drew on the beach… I never really understood what they were for. What practical purpose did they serve out here?
day_5.response: None, practically. But I think that was kind of the point. Not everything out here had to be practical. The flowers were just DaVinci being DaVinci, keeping himself human through all of it. Honestly looking back I think that mattered more than I gave it credit for at the time.

day_5.utterance: *His cheering stops. He looks over at you, notices you haven't moved, and the smile slowly fades. He waits.*
day_5.response: Just give me a second. I don't know why I can't move. It's right there.

day_5.utterance: Rescue is here… they're waving us over. Are you going? I'll follow you.
